Not everyone knows this (and I certainly don't pretend to), but Apple has actually published extremely detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of devices, helping accessory manufacturers design compatible products. Here are the details.

Apple hardware, fully exposed

For nearly three decades, Jason Kottke has been one of my primary sources for discovering interesting things on the internet (and beyond), and I'm sure there are plenty of things I would never have found without him.

A few days ago, he posted a link to the "Dimensional Drawings" section within the Accessories section of the Apple developer website.

In short, it's a repository of highly detailed technical drawings, currently covering 96 devices, including the brand-new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like the MacBook Neo and Siri Remote, as well as accessories like AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and Apple Vision Pro ZEISS optical insert accessories.

Each document contains precise measurements ranging from overall device dimensions and curves to buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers and ports, along with detailed "keepout zone" markings indicating where certain materials cannot be placed.

Although these documents are primarily intended for accessory manufacturers, anyone with even a passing interest in hardware, industrial design, or even just the meticulous qualities of Apple products should find them worth a look.

To view Apple's dimensional drawings, please follow this link. If you're not already following kottke.org, you should start right away.
